Pretty much any VPN is going to add lag to your gameplay, at the very best they add only one hop to the trip between you and the server. They may be useful if you want to buy a game and look like you are from another country but I can't think of a single time where using your connection to hook to another connection and then going from there out to the server is going to make the trip shorter. I just don't see the purpose for a VPN when gaming.

Forcing your traffice route is a thing, to be honest for 99 percent of gamers it will not make a difference. There are some hops that are slower than others. Using a VPN to force a different hop is something I have seen "professional" lol players do to drop jitter and ping by small amounts (like 1-3%) is the maximum I saw. Not truly worth it. The only other reason is if priority traffic is enforced. Netflix and other streaming media are usually prioritized because that is what most people use the net for daily. Also sites like speedtest are prioritized to give better results. VPNs mask the connection (assuming you are using the VPN dns, sometimes it is a fight, there are several companies that try to fight for control of your dns) and may help with prioritization.

The thing is the VPN doesn't change the route adds a stop along the way and masks the traffic, even taking an existing direct path of hops from a to b if you add a middle point already along the way it doesn't make it less hops and the hardware relaying the signal causes you the most delay, adding encryption and decryption through a middle hop that was not part of the direct path is not going to make things faster, in fact the extra processing will slow you down and add load to your system in the background. the only thing I could see it avoiding is priority traffic, and I would have expected the extra load and hops to have end up equaling out any minor gains from bypassing that.
